strategy.thesis: Medibank is Australia's largest private health insurer; its internal Ventures function builds, buys and invests in health products and services (spanning Medibank, ahm and Amplar brands) to drive preventative and integrated care for its ~10 million customers, with disclosed focus areas including mental health, obesity and pain management.

summary.en: Corporate venturing and M&A arm of Medibank Private, Australia's largest health insurer, that invests in and acquires health-tech companies (e.g. telehealth platform Medinet) to expand virtual and preventative care for its members.

sources.title: Medibank invests $10 million in health tech company Medinet
sources.supports: Medibank's $10M investment in health tech company Medinet, part of its Ventures strategy
sources.quote: Medibank invested $10 million in health tech company Medinet to support the growing role of virtual health in Australia

sources.title: RT New Ventures – Medibank
sources.supports: Existence and mandate of Medibank's Ventures function
sources.quote: Medibank's Ventures group builds, buys, and invests in amazing health products and services to grow Medibank's impact to 10 million Australians by 2030.

verification_notes: Medibank later moved from minority investment to 100% acquisition of Medinet (announced separately). Ventures activity is run as an internal corporate function rather than a formally named external fund.

strategy.thesis: ASX-listed health insurer nib makes direct corporate investments and joint ventures in digital-health and virtual-care companies as part of its 'payer to partner' strategy to move beyond indemnity insurance into care delivery and data-driven prevention.

summary.en: nib, an Australian ASX-listed private health insurer, invests directly in health-tech startups (e.g. a 50% stake in digital pharmacy Midnight Health via $4M then a $12M Series A) and has formed health-data joint ventures such as with Cigna, as part of its strategic shift from payer to health-services partner.

sources.title: Nic Blair's digital healthcare startup Midnight Health scores $4m investment from nib
sources.supports: nib's $4M investment for a 50% stake in Midnight Health
sources.quote: nib (ASX: NHF) invested $4 million in digital healthcare startup Midnight Health, securing a 50 percent stake in the medication delivery company.

sources.title: Insurer nib backs Queensland startup Midnight Health in $12 million Series A
sources.supports: nib's follow-on $12M Series A investment in Midnight Health
sources.quote: Insurer nib backs Queensland startup Midnight Health in $12 million Series A

sources.title: nib and Cigna create health services joint venture
sources.supports: nib and Cigna $10M-each joint venture on disease-risk analytics
sources.quote: nib and Cigna established a joint venture with each contributing $10 million in startup funding.

verification_notes: nib does not appear to run a formally branded 'nib Ventures' fund; investments are made directly by the corporate group (nib holdings / nib Health Funds).

aka: Hospitals Contribution Fund of Australia - Catalyst

strategy.thesis: HCF, Australia's largest not-for-profit health fund, runs the Catalyst health-tech accelerator (with Slingshot) and has made strategic-investor commitments into dedicated health/wellness venture capital (e.g. XT Ventures) to seed innovation relevant to its members.

summary.en: Not-for-profit health insurer HCF backs Australian health, wellness and fitness innovation through its Catalyst accelerator program (55 graduates since 2015) and as a cornerstone AU$5M investor in XT Ventures, described as Australia's first dedicated health/wellness/sport venture capital fund.

sources.title: About HCF Catalyst: Driving Innovation in Health Tech
sources.supports: HCF Catalyst program description and 2015 founding via Slingshot partnership
sources.quote: HCF Catalyst is Australia's first corporate supported health tech accelerator program.

sources.title: HCF invests $5 million in Australia's first venture capitalist fund for health, wellness, sport and fitness start-ups
sources.supports: HCF's AU$5M cornerstone investment in XT Ventures
sources.quote: Private health insurer HCF has announced an AU$5 million (US$3.5 million) investment in XT Ventures, the nation's first venture capitalist fund for start-ups in the health, wellness, sport and fitness sector.

sources.title: How HCF Catalyst is driving innovation in health tech
sources.supports: Catalyst program track record of 55 startups/scaleups and $25M+ funding raised by graduates
sources.quote: startups that have come through the Catalyst program have attracted more than $25 million in funding, with 55 startups and scaleups graduating and moving forward with their businesses

verification_notes: HCF's own capital is deployed both as accelerator seed funding ($50K per Catalyst cohort company) and as an LP-style cornerstone investment into the independently managed XT Ventures fund; HCF does not itself directly hold XT Ventures' portfolio stakes.

strategy.thesis: Bupa Ventures is the corporate venture fund of Bupa Asia Pacific, the region's arm of the global healthcare and insurance group Bupa; it backs seed-to-Series-A startups in predictive/preventative healthcare, genomics and personalised medicine, and home/remote care monitoring to make healthcare more personal and less fragmented for Bupa's members.

summary.en: Bupa Ventures is the AU$20M corporate venture fund of Bupa Asia Pacific (the ANZ-region arm of global healthcare group Bupa), investing in seed/Series-A startups spanning predictive and preventative healthcare, genomics and personalised medicine, and remote care; first cheques went to Umps Health, Vively Health and Eugene Labs.

sources.title: Bupa Ventures to invest $20m to accelerate healthcare innovations
sources.supports: AU$20M fund size and focus areas
sources.quote: Bupa announced the launch of a new $20 million Bupa Ventures Fund to support and invest in start-ups that are focused on developing innovative models of healthcare that enable better health outcomes.

sources.title: Bupa Ventures announces first investments
sources.supports: First portfolio companies: Umps Health, Vively Health, Eugene Labs
sources.quote: Bupa Ventures announces its first round of early-stage investments through its Ventures Fund with Umps Health, Vively Health, and Eugene Labs sharing in ~AU$2.2 million in investment.

verification_notes: Bupa's global HQ is in the UK (Bupa is not medically-core in the sense of being a hospital/pharma operator — it is an international health insurer/aged-care group); Bupa Ventures specifically funds and operates out of Bupa Asia Pacific, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. An earlier globalventuring.com report cited a smaller AU$13m figure for the fund; AU$20m is the figure given directly on Bupa's own newsroom.

strategy.thesis: HBF Ventures is the newly launched (Feb 2026) A$25M corporate venture fund of Perth-based not-for-profit health insurer HBF, targeting digital health and advanced analytics, new care-delivery models, and preventative/population health services, explicitly prioritising member health outcomes over pure financial return.

summary.en: HBF Ventures is a A$25 million corporate venture fund launched in February 2026 by Perth health insurer HBF, managed via Artesian's Venture Capital as a Service model, targeting digital health, new care-delivery models and preventative/population health startups over a planned 15-20 investment, 10-year program.

sources.title: HBF launches new $25 million fund to back health innovation
sources.supports: A$25M fund size, launch, focus areas
sources.quote: Perth-based HBF unveiled HBF Ventures on February 9, 2026—a A$25 million dedicated fund targeting health tech startups that could redefine care delivery for its 1 million+ members.

sources.title: HBF Health Tech Fund Launch Signals Insurer Shift Into VC
sources.supports: 10-year horizon, 15-20 planned investments, Artesian VCaaS management
sources.quote: HBF Ventures has a 10-year investment horizon and expects to make between 15 and 20 investments over its lifecycle, established using capital from the company's existing investment portfolio... Artesian—a top-tier early-stage VC with A$2 billion+ under management—will manage the fund via its "Venture Capital as a Service" (VCaaS) model.

verification_notes: Very recently launched (Feb 2026); no portfolio companies disclosed yet at time of research.

strategy.thesis: W23 is the corporate venture arm of Woolworths Group, Australia's largest supermarket retailer; it invests in retail-tech, climate-tech and digital health, complementing Woolworths' HealthyLife health-and-wellness subsidiary, which has itself led venture investment (e.g. into telehealth provider Hola Health).

summary.en: W23 is Woolworths Group's corporate venture capital arm (est. 2019), investing across retail-tech, climate-tech and digital health; Woolworths' health-and-wellness subsidiary HealthyLife separately led a $10M Series A into telehealth platform Hola Health to become its exclusive telehealth provider.

sources.title: W23 investment portfolio
sources.supports: W23 founding year (2019), HQ location, and sector focus including digital health
sources.quote: Woolworths established a venture capital arm called W23 in April 2019. W23 is the corporate venture arm of Woolworths Group based in Baulkham Hills, Australia, and seeks to invest in retail-tech, climate-tech, and digital health.

sources.title: Hola Health secures $10 million led by Woolworths Group subsidiary
sources.supports: HealthyLife (Woolworths subsidiary) leading a $10M Series A in Hola Health telehealth
sources.quote: Healthylife, a Woolworths Group subsidiary, led a Series A round investment to establish Hola as Healthylife's exclusive telehealth provider through the "Hola by Telehealth" platform.

verification_notes: The Hola Health investment was made by HealthyLife (a wholly-owned Woolworths operating subsidiary), not confirmed to be booked directly through the W23 fund vehicle; both are treated here as part of Woolworths Group's broader corporate health-investment activity.

strategy.thesis: Telstra Health is the dedicated health-technology investment and acquisition arm of Telstra, Australia's largest telecommunications company; it grows a portfolio of clinical software, e-prescribing and care-coordination businesses via majority/full acquisitions rather than classic minority-stake VC checks.

summary.en: Telstra Health is telecom giant Telstra's dedicated healthcare investment and M&A division, having made 7 acquisitions of Australian and international health IT companies including MedicalDirector ($350M, 2021), a 70% stake in PowerHealth ($95M, 2024), and full ownership of pharmacy-IT provider Fred IT Group (2024).

sources.title: Telstra Health acquires MedicalDirector for the digital future of health care
sources.supports: MedicalDirector acquisition for $350M in 2021
sources.quote: Telstra Health acquired leading GP clinical and practice management software company MedicalDirector for $350m.

sources.title: Telstra Health to fully own pharma tech provider Fred IT
sources.supports: Full acquisition of Fred IT Group, pharmacy sector IT provider
sources.quote: Telstra Health will fully acquire Fred IT Group, Australia's leading provider of IT solutions for the pharmacy sector.

sources.title: Telstra Health announces major investment in global healthcare organisation PowerHealth
sources.supports: 70% stake in PowerHealth for $95M in 2024
sources.quote: In July 2024, Telstra Health acquired a 70 per cent stake in PowerHealth for $95m.

verification_notes: Telstra Health operates predominantly through full/majority acquisitions and buy-and-build rather than a formal minority-stake CVC fund; included here as the dedicated health-investment division of a non-medical (telecom) parent, per slice scope. HQ city inferred from Telstra's general Melbourne base, not independently confirmed for Telstra Health specifically.

strategy.thesis: Wesfarmers Health is the dedicated health division of Wesfarmers, a diversified Australian retail/industrial conglomerate; it acquires and builds digital-health, pharmacy-retail and medical-aesthetics businesses (Priceline Pharmacy, API, SILK Laser, Clear Skincare, InstantScripts, SiSU Health) as a non-medical-core corporate's health investment arm.

summary.en: Wesfarmers Health, formed in 2022 within diversified conglomerate Wesfarmers (owner of Bunnings, Kmart, Officeworks), invests in and acquires digital-health and pharmacy-adjacent businesses, notably buying telehealth provider InstantScripts for $135M and fully acquiring in-store health-screening kiosk operator SiSU Health.

sources.title: Wesfarmers Health
sources.supports: Wesfarmers Health division formed 2022, business units including digital health
sources.quote: Wesfarmers Health was formed as a division of Wesfarmers in 2022, with the acquisition of API and brands including Priceline Pharmacy and Clear Skincare, and the business has expanded its footprint with further acquisitions in the digital health and medical aesthetics industries.

sources.title: Wesfarmers Health to acquire InstantScripts for $135 million
sources.supports: InstantScripts acquisition price of $135M
sources.quote: Wesfarmers agreed to buy digital health business InstantScripts for $135 million, adding the telehealth firm to the Wesfarmers Health division.

verification_notes: Wesfarmers Health invests via full-ownership acquisitions rather than minority VC stakes; included as the health-investment arm of a non-medical (diversified retail/industrial) parent, consistent with slice scope.

strategy.thesis: IAG Firemark Ventures is the corporate venture capital arm of Insurance Australia Group, primarily focused on insurtech/fintech; it also makes targeted investments where mental-health and medical-support technology intersects with insurance claims prevention, e.g. its minority investment in crisis-support platform Sonder.

notable_investments.sector: mental health / medical & safety support app

summary.en: IAG Firemark Ventures, the CVC arm of general insurer Insurance Australia Group, is primarily an insurtech investor but made a strategic minority investment in Sonder, a 24/7 mental-health, medical and safety support app, to extend crisis and psychological-harm support to IAG policyholders.

sources.title: IAG invests in Sonder to bring early intervention and immediate care to customers
sources.supports: IAG Firemark Ventures' minority investment in mental-health platform Sonder
sources.quote: Insurance Australia Group (IAG) has made a strategic investment in Sonder, a platform that provides real-time mental health, medical, and safety assistance, through Firemark Ventures, IAG's corporate venture capital arm.

sources.title: Firemark Ventures | IAG's Corporate Venture Capital Fund
sources.supports: Firemark Ventures identified as IAG's CVC fund
sources.quote: Firemark Ventures | IAG's Corporate Venture Capital Fund

verification_notes: Firemark Ventures' core mandate is insurtech/fintech, not healthcare; included here on the strength of its verified direct investment in mental-health/medical-support platform Sonder. Most of its broader portfolio is out of scope for this medical-VC directory.

strategy.thesis: Ki Tua is the corporate venture arm of Fonterra, New Zealand's largest company and a dairy co-operative; it invests in food, agtech and nutrition-science startups beyond Fonterra's core dairy business, including microbiome-derived metabolic healthcare technology, to future-proof the business with adjacent bio-science bets.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Co-develops microbiome-derived products with portfolio companies such as Pendulum, linking Fonterra's dairy/nutrition science base to human metabolic-health applications.

summary.en: Ki Tua (originally Nutrition Science Solutions) is the corporate venture fund of Fonterra, New Zealand's largest dairy co-operative; it manages over $100M and made a $10M investment in Pendulum, a San Francisco microbiome-derived metabolic healthcare technology company, alongside food/agtech bets, as part of Fonterra's move beyond core dairy.

sources.title: Fonterra sets up a new corporate venture arm
sources.supports: Fonterra's formation of a corporate venture arm (provisionally Nutrition Science Solutions, later renamed Ki Tua)
sources.quote: Fonterra, a dairy cooperative and the largest company in New Zealand, has formed a corporate venture capital subsidiary provisionally called Nutrition Science Solutions (NSS).

sources.title: New Zealand dairy company Fonterra targets microbiome investments
sources.supports: $10M investment in microbiome-derived metabolic healthcare company Pendulum
sources.quote: The fund announced a $10m investment in Pendulum, a San Francisco-based microbiome-derived metabolic healthcare technology company, and Fonterra partnered with the company to co-develop microbiome products and expand globally.

sources.title: Fonterra launches new nutrition science venture arm; announces first investment
sources.supports: Official Fonterra confirmation of the venture arm and its nutrition-science focus
sources.quote: Fonterra launches new nutrition science venture arm; announces first investment

verification_notes: Ki Tua's portfolio spans food/agtech broadly, with Pendulum as its clearest verified medical/health-tech nexus (human metabolic healthcare); other portfolio companies (e.g. BioLumic) are agricultural/plant-science rather than human health.
